english_title: Proposition 0, CMC Mathematics Group Senior Final Problem
statement_en:
Let $(X,\Omega,\mu)$ be a measure space, and let $f_n$ be a sequence of measurable functions on $X$ that is almost everywhere uniformly bounded. Define $A_N(x):=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\leq N} f_n(x)$. Then
$$\sum_{N\geq 1} \frac{1}{N}\int_X A_{N}^{2}(x)\,d\mu <\infty\implies A_N(x)\xrightarrow{a.e.}{0}.$$
